reasoning: compute_local() begins 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(); return; }' (impl header lines 156-162). I read src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.h: the class declares only 'void init() override; void compute_local() override; double memory_usage() override;' - no compute_array. Its base src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.h declares 'void compute_local() override = 0;' and no compute_array. So the qualified call resolves to Compute's 'virtual void compute_array() {}' (src/compute.h:129) - an empty body. host_flag is set from 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK)'; src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.cpp instantiates ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkosDevice<LMPDeviceType> unconditionally, and on a CPU-only Kokkos build LMPDeviceType==LMPHostType so execution_space==HostKK and the branch is taken. The contrast the finding draws is real: ComputeSNAGrid does declare 'void compute_array() override;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.h:32), so the sibling compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h host branch is correct. Nothing else fills alocal on the host path - setup() only create_kokkos()es it (NoInit is not used there but memoryKK create is uninitialized malloc), so dump local prints whatever is in memory.
fix: In ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkos::compute_local(), change the host branch to 'ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_local(); return;'. Note the base compute_local() writes into alocal[igrid][...], and alocal here points into the Kokkos view host data, so also mark k_alocal.modify_host() (or simply keep the host path entirely on the base-class allocation, see F0072).

reasoning: Same defect as F0065 (duplicate), and the extra claim about the sibling checks out too. src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:128-132 reads 'void ComputeGaussianGridLocalKokkos<DeviceType>::compute_local() { if (host_flag) { return; } invoked_local = update->ntimestep; ...' - it returns before computing anything, so on a CPU-only Kokkos build gaussian/grid/local/kk likewise leaves alocal unwritten and does not even set invoked_local. reasoning: TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh has two loops 'for (int j = 0; j < ntotal; j++)' (counting pass and fill pass); neither tests atom->mask. The constructor sets 'datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK;' and compute_local() syncs only X_MASK|F_MASK|TYPE_MASK, so mask is never even fetched. The CPU original src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp compute_local() has, as the first statement of the identical j loop, 'if (!(mask[j] & groupbit)) continue;' with 'const int *const mask = atom->mask;' hoisted above. No compensating filter exists anywhere else in the KOKKOS path - the fill kernel TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill only copies blist into alocal. So for any group other than 'all' the /kk descriptors include out-of-group atoms.
fix: Add MASK_MASK to datamask_read and to the atomKK->sync() in compute_local(); add 'mask = atomKK->k_mask.view<DeviceType>();' next to the x/type captures, declare the view in compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.h, and add 'if (!(mask(j) & groupbit)) continue;' as the first statement of both j loops in TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh.

reasoning: Constructor: 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1]; for (i=1..ntypes) for (j=1..ntypes) { k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... }' - every entry of the (ntypes+1)^2 table gets cutsq[1][1]. The base class really does build a per-type table: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp constructor, 'cut = 2.0*radelem[i]*rcutfac; cutsq[i][i] = cut*cut;' plus the off-diagonal '(radelem[i]+radelem[j])*rcutfac'. And the kernel compounds it: TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh uses 'rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)' with 'const int itype = 1;' hard-wired a few lines above, i.e. row 1 only, while the CPU cutoff test is 'if (rsq < cutsq[jtype][jtype] && rsq > 1e-20)'. Both halves of the finding hold; with a single atom type the two agree, with differing radelem they do not.
fix: Fill k_cutsq from the real base-class table ('k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = cutsq[i][j];' inside the double loop, then modify_host()), and change both kernel tests to 'rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype)' to match compute_sna_grid_local.cpp. Drop the now-unused cutsq_tmp member.

reasoning: compute_local() has '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.' followed by 'max_neighs = 100;', and then 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);' (the line 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, ntotal);' is commented out directly above it). TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh's second loop runs over all ntotal atoms and writes 'snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0..2)', 'snaKK.wj(ii,offset)', 'snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset)', 'snaKK.inside(ii,offset)' then 'offset++' with no comparison against max_neighs anywhere. The CPU style sizes for the worst case: 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'. The scratch allocation is also sized 'team_size_compute_neigh * max_neighs'. Two separate consequences: >100 neighbours writes out of bounds, and the downstream ComputeCayleyKlein/ComputeUi range policies are built with extent max_neighs so neighbours 100+ would be silently skipped even if the memory were large enough (d_ninside(ii) is stored unclamped and used as the loop bound in those kernels).
fix: Add a max-reduction over d_ninside (or a cheap pre-pass counting atoms within cutmax of each grid point), take the MPI-local max, and pass that to grow_rij; alternatively pass ntotal as the commented-out line did. As a minimum, clamp offset and raise an error when ninside > max_neighs.

reasoning: All three TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi operator() overloads (3-index, 2-index and 1-index forms) contain 'int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);'. iatom is 'iatom_mod + iatom_div*vector_length' bounded by 'if (iatom >= chunk_size) return;' - chunk_size is MIN(chunksize, total_range) grid points, not atoms. The same file states the intended convention in TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh: '// currently, all grid points are type 1 ... const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', which matches the CPU code 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = map[itype];'. Two failures: (a) the central element is map[type[grid_index]] instead of map[1]; (b) d_map is read even when chemflag is 0, and MemKK::realloc_kokkos uses 'Kokkos::NoInit' (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:429) and d_map is deep-copied only 'if (chemflag)', so with chemflag off ielem is garbage. Also type() has extent nmax, so chunk_size > nmax is an out-of-bounds read. One of these is dispatched for every run - snap_get_policy picks the overload by policy rank at compute_local().
fix: In all three TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi overloads replace the two lines with 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;' (matching the ComputeNeigh convention and the CPU style). Optionally hoist it to a member computed once in compute_local().

reasoning: Constructor: 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,...,nelements); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_wjelem,...,nelements); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_sinnerelem,...,nelements); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_dinnerelem,...,nelements);' then host mirrors are filled by 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag) { h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. nelements is 1 unless the 'chem' keyword is given (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp sets 'nelements = 1;' in the defaults block and only reassigns it under 'chem'), and it is unrelated to atom->ntypes. Both halves of the claim hold: (a) ntypes > nelements overruns radelem/wjelem, (b) the sinner/dinner writes use index i (1..ntypes) into a length-nelements view, so even ntypes==nelements==1 writes h_sinnerelem(1) one past the end. These are host mirror views allocated with Kokkos::NoInit, so this is a plain heap overflow with no bounds check in a release build.
fix: Size all four views with atom->ntypes (they are indexed by type, not element - see F0077) or with MAX(nelements, atom->ntypes) if the element indexing is kept, and use the same i-1 offset for sinner/dinner as for radelem/wjelem.

reasoning: setup() is 'ComputeGridLocal::setup(); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal"); array_local = alocal; d_alocal = ...'. src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp: setup() = 'deallocate(); set_grid_global(); set_grid_local(); allocate(); assign_coords();'; allocate() = 'gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...); array_local = alocal;'; deallocate() = 'if (gridlocal_allocated) { gridlocal_allocated = 0; memory->destroy(alocal); }'. MemoryKokkos::create_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&, n1, n2, name) (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h) smalloc()s only the row-pointer array and sets 'array[i] = &h_data(i,0)', i.e. row 0 points into the Kokkos View's host allocation. Memory::destroy(TYPE**&) does 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);'. So on the second setup() (Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() on every run) deallocate() free()s a pointer that was never malloc()ed. The leak of the base-class array on the first setup() is real too. The sibling confirms the intent: compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h setup() opens with '// Do not call ComputeGrid::setup(), we don't wanna allocate the grid array there.' and calls only set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(). The same pattern (ComputeGridLocal::setup() followed by create_kokkos) is in src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp setup(), whose destructor even has a commented-out '//gridlocal_allocated = 0;'.
fix: Replace 'ComputeGridLocal::setup();' with 'ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global(); ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_local();' (mirroring compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h), then memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal) before create_kokkos, and leave gridlocal_allocated at 0 so the base deallocate() is a no-op. Grid coordinate columns are already written by TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh, so the dropped assign_coords() is not needed on the device path. Apply the identical change in compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp.

reasoning: TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh fill loop: 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac;' with a comment admitting the choice ('pair snap uses jelem here, but we use jtype, see compute_sna_grid.cpp / actually since the views here have values starting at 0, let's use jelem'). The CPU original is unambiguous: 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac;'. So whenever two types map to the same element they get identical weights/radii on the device but distinct ones on the CPU. The off-by-one interaction is real as well: the mirrors were filled with h_wjelem(i-1)=wjelem[i], so with chemflag off (jelem always 0) every neighbour gets wjelem[1]/radelem[1] regardless of type. Note the neighbouring sinnerij/dinnerij lines diverge from the CPU too (KOKKOS averages ielem and jelem, the CPU uses sinnerelem[jelem] alone), which is a further instance of the same class of defect.
fix: Index by type: 'snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jtype-1]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = 2.0*d_radelem[jtype-1]*rcutfac;' after sizing d_wjelem/d_radelem with atom->ntypes (see F0070), or drop the -1 offset and size them ntypes+1 so the indexing reads like the CPU code. Also reconcile sinnerij/dinnerij with compute_sna_grid_local.cpp.

reasoning: ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkos::compute_local() starts with the host_flag branch and then 'copymode = 1; zlen = ...' - there is no 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;' anywhere in the function (grep over the whole impl header finds no invoked_local). reasoning: KOKKOS kernel: 'const KK_FLOAT imass = rmass[i];' ... 'const KK_FLOAT jmass = rmass[j];' ... 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass); if (mask_i & freeze_group_bit) meff = jmass; if (mask[j] & freeze_group_bit) meff = imass;'. The CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp has, under the comment '// meff = effective mass of pair of particles / if I or J part of rigid body, use body mass': 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; } meff = mi*mj/(mi+mj);', and the top of PairGranHooke::compute() refreshes mass_rigid from fix_rigid->extract("body")/extract("masstotal") on every reneighbor followed by comm->forward_comm(this). 'grep -n "mass_rigid\|fix_rigid" src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*' returns nothing, so no compensating path exists. PairGranHookeKokkos::init_style() calls PairGranHooke::init_style() (which reaches PairGranHookeHistory::init_style where fix_rigid is looked up and assigned) and then only adjusts the neighbor request and rejects FULL lists - there is no guard rejecting fix_rigid. meff feeds both the normal damping 'damp = meff*gamman_kk*vnnr*rsqinv' and the friction cap 'fs = meff*gammat_kk*vrel', so the divergence changes forces.
fix: Port the rigid-body mass path: add a DAT::tdual_float_1d k_mass_rigid filled in compute() when (fix_rigid && neighbor->ago == 0) from fix_rigid->extract("body")/("masstotal") plus the existing forward_comm, sync it to the device, and in the kernel use 'KK_FLOAT mi = imass, mj = jmass; if (fix_rigid_flag) { if (d_mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = d_mass_rigid[i]; if (d_mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = d_mass_rigid[j]; }' before forming meff. Apply to all three KOKKOS granular styles (see F0499). As an interim measure, add 'if (fix_rigid) error->all(FLERR,"Pair style gran/hooke/kk does not (yet) support fix rigid");' at the end of init_style().

reasoning: Same defect as F0334, verified to span all three styles. Identical 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass); if (mask_i & freeze_group_bit) meff = jmass; if (mask[j] & freeze_group_bit) meff = imass;' appears at pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:280, pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:350 and pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:350, with imass/jmass taken from rmass in every case. Grep for mass_rigid or fix_rigid across all six src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_* files finds no hits. The CPU counterparts pair_gran_hooke.cpp and pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp both do the mass_rigid substitution (pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:237 'if (fix_rigid) {' guards the same block, and hertz/history inherits that compute()). In hertz/history and hooke/history meff additionally enters the shear-history update ('shear1 = (fn/fs)*(shear1 + meff*gammat_kk*vtr1/kt_kk) - meff*gammat_kk*vtr1/kt_kk'), so the error accumulates in the stored history, not just the instantaneous force.
fix: See F0334; make the same change in pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp and pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp.

reasoning: src/pair.h:247 declares 'int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos'. Neither pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.h nor pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.h nor pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.h declares a shadowing member (grep for special_lj in those three headers returns nothing), while pair_lj_cut_kokkos.h:91 and pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.h:89 both declare 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];'. So the four assignments in compute() ('special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...') convert force->special_lj's doubles to int. The kernel then reads 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]); ... if (factor_lj == 0) continue;' and, further down, actually scales with it ('fx *= factor_lj; ... tor3 *= factor_lj;'), exactly like the CPU style which uses 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;'. So a factor of 0.5 becomes 0 and the pair is skipped entirely; 1.5 would become 1. Reachability requires bonded granular particles (e.g. atom_style hybrid sphere bond) with a fractional special_bonds lj factor, which is why I keep this at medium rather than high, but the truncation itself is unambiguous. All three KOKKOS granular styles are affected identically (lines 125-128 / 142-145 / 142-145).
fix: Add 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' as a protected member of PairGranHookeKokkos, PairGranHookeHistoryKokkos and PairGranHertzHistoryKokkos (shadowing Pair::special_lj the way pair_lj_cut_kokkos.h does), so the four copies in compute() keep full precision.
